outputs.exact_statement: Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface. Suppose that, for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, one rational polarization, and one full even-Clifford realization, the tensor of $j_w(v)(a)=vaw$ is induced by a cycle in $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S\times A^2)_{\mathbb Q}$. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power of $S$.

Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface. Suppose that there is a rational isometric embedding $$(T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P.$$ For any full even-Clifford realization $H^1(A,\mathbb Q)=C^+(T_S,q)$, any rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, and any rational polarization $E$ of this weight-one Hodge structure, there is a cycle $$\Gamma_S\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S\times A\times A)_{\mathbb Q}$$ whose action on every $x\in T_S$ is exactly $\iota_{w,E}(x)$ in $H^2(A\times A,\mathbb Q)$. The same assertion holds on a transported isogenous model with its specified tensor.*

*Moreover, the rational Hodge conjecture and the rational generalized Hodge conjecture hold in every cohomological degree of every self-power $S^m$, for every integer $m\ge1$.

There is a primitive embedding of $P$ in $\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}}=\mathbb U^{\oplus3}\oplus E_8(-1)^{\oplus2}$ with orthogonal complement $T_P=\mathbb U\oplus\mathbb U(2)\oplus D_4(-1)$. For every primitive embedding of $P$ in the K3 lattice, the rational orthogonal complement is isometric to $V_P$.

Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface with transcendental space $(T,q)$ of rational dimension $t$, put $V=T(1)$, and let $W=C^+(T,q)=H^1(A,\mathbb Q)$ be an even-Clifford Kuga–Satake realization. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T$ the tensor form of $$\label{ext:exact-kappa}
 j_w:V\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(W),\qquad
 j_w(v)(a)=vaw,$$ is induced by a cycle in $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S\times A^2)_{\mathbb Q}$, using a rational polarization of $W$. Then, for every $1\leq k\leq t$, there is an injective algebraic Hodge map $$F_k:\bigwedge^kV\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(W)$$ with an algebraic left inverse on cohomology. More precisely, put $Z=A^2$ and $n=\dim Z$. There are correspondences $$\Gamma_k\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^{k+1}(S^k\times Z)_\mathbb Q,\qquad
 R_k\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^{n+k-1}(Z\times S^k)_\mathbb Q.$$ Viewing $\bigwedge^kV$ in $H^{2k}(S^k,\mathbb Q)(k)$ and identifying $\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(W)\simeq(H^1(A,\mathbb Q)\otimes H^1(A,\mathbb Q))(1)\subset H^2(Z,\mathbb Q)(1)$ by a rational polarization, their weight-zero actions satisfy $(\Gamma_k)_*|_{\wedge^kV}=F_k$ and $(R_k)_*F_k=\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$. Every rational Hodge class in $\bigwedge^kV$ is the class of a rational algebraic cycle of codimension $k$ on $S^k$.

Let $X,Y$ be smooth projective varieties, with $\dim X=N$ and $\dim Y=D$, and let $C\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^{N+p}(X\times Y)_\mathbb Q$, where $p\ge0$. There is a fixed closed subset $B\subset Y$ of codimension at least $p$ supporting the image of $C_*$ on cohomology. In particular, $$C_*H^j(X,\mathbb Q)\subset N^pH^{j+2p}(Y,\mathbb Q).$$

Let $S$ satisfy the exact even-Clifford algebraicity hypothesis of Proposition 4, and put $t=\dim_\mathbb QT$. For every $1\le k\le t$, $$\bigwedge^kT\subset N^{k-1}H^{2k}(S^k,\mathbb Q).$$ Moreover every rational sub-Hodge structure of this exterior power satisfies the generalized Hodge conjecture in its ambient $H^{2k}(S^k,\mathbb Q)$. In particular, the top exterior line is supported in codimension $t$.

Let $V=T(1)$ for a projective K3 surface with $\operatorname{Hg}(V)=\mathop{\mathrm{SO}}(V,q)$ and $t=\dim V\ge3$. Let $H$ be a nontrivial rational simple representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of $V$, endowed with its induced weight-zero Hodge structure. If its Hodge level is at most $2b$, there are integers $c,s\ge1$ and $k_1,\ldots,k_c\ge1$ such that $$c\le b,\qquad s=\sum_i k_i,\qquad k_i\le t,
 \qquad \bigotimes_{i=1}^c\bigwedge^{k_i}V\longrightarrow H$$ is a surjective rational Hodge map.

Let $V=T(1)$ for a projective K3 surface and let $G=\operatorname{Hg}(V)$. If a nontrivial rational simple representation $H$ occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of $V$ has induced Hodge level at most $2b$, then there are $1\le c\le b$ and $1\le k_1,\ldots,k_c\le\dim_\mathbb QV$ with a surjective rational Hodge map $$\bigotimes_{j=1}^c\bigwedge^{k_j}V\longrightarrow H.$$

There is a smooth double cover $Y\to K=\mathop{\mathrm{Km}}(B')$, with $K$ the resolved Kummer surface, satisfying the following assertions.*

1.  *The anti-invariant lattice $$V=H^2(Y,\mathbb Z)^{\delta=-1}$$ (with torsion removed) is even, has signature $(2,14)$, and has $2$-elementary discriminant group. For fixed $(B,M,\chi)$, monodromy acts trivially on this discriminant group.*

2.  *There are eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes $a_1,\ldots,a_8$, each of square $-4$. Their perpendicular $$U=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_8\rangle^\perp\subset V_\mathbb Q$$ is a Hodge structure of signature $(2,6)$ and, with the intersection form inherited from $Y$, is rationally isometric to $$V_P=(\mathbb U\oplus\mathbb U(2)\oplus D_4(-1))_\mathbb Q.$$*


3.  *Resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism $\beta:U\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X$ with $$(\beta x,\beta y)_X=2(x,y)_Y.$$ The algebraic projector $$\label{geom:projector}
     e=\frac14(\Delta_X+\Gamma_j-\Gamma_\delta-\Gamma_{j\delta})
           \in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(X\times X)_\mathbb Q$$ has image $U_X$ in degree two and is zero in every other degree.*

*The constructions are compatible with variation on the indicated smooth parameter opens.

The period map of $U$, equivalently of $U_X$, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For a very general parameter, its rational Hodge structure is simple, has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, and has Hodge group $\mathop{\mathrm{SO}}(U)$.

For $(B,D)$ in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the parameter space, $D$ has no nontrivial translation stabilizer. Its quotient $C=D/\{\pm1\}$ is a smooth genus-three curve, and the connected étale cover $D\to C$ is defined by a nontrivial line bundle $\epsilon\in\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}^0(C)[2]$. The Gauss map is the composite $$D\longrightarrow C\xrightarrow{|K_C\otimes\epsilon|}\mathbf P^1,$$ of degrees two and four. No fiber of the degree-four map has all its multiplicities even. The good open remains nonempty on every connected component obtained by adjoining the finite theta, torsion, and level choices used to define $X$.

There is an algebraic map $h:\mathcal S\to B$ such that $$\label{geom:coherent}
 2h(s)=\sum_{p\in s}p,\qquad h(s[p])=h(s)-p.$$ The selections split globally into two degree-eight covers $\mathcal S_+\sqcup\mathcal S_-$ according to the parity of the number of sign changes. Their smooth projective completions $C_\pm$, which may be disconnected, carry extensions $a_\pm:C_\pm\to B$ of $h$. Wherever its differential is nonzero, either map is tangent to the direction recorded by its parameter in $\mathbf P^1$.

On a regular-value disc, no signed sum of a nonempty subset of the four local branches $x_i$ is constant. Every connected component of $C_+$ and $C_-$ maps nonconstantly to $B$. No image component from $C_+$ is an opposite translate of an image component from $C_-$; that is, their image curves cannot satisfy $Z_+=b-Z_-$ for any $b\in B$.

For every parameter in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the parameter space, there exist smooth projective connected curves $C_1,C_2$ and a dominant generically finite morphism $$g:C_1\times C_2\longrightarrow X.$$ Whenever additionally $U_X$ has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, an algebraic correspondence induces an injection $$U_X\hookrightarrow H^1(C_1,\mathbb Q)\otimes H^1(C_2,\mathbb Q).$$ In particular, this injection exists at a very general parameter.

Every nonempty regular period chart admits a smaller normalized product chart $A\times Q$ of abelian data and affine section coordinates as in Section [geom:section-charts], mapping into it and lying in the simultaneous geometric open of Propositions 11 and 15. For any prescribed countable collection of proper closed analytic period loci in the original chart, the following choices are available in this order:* 1. *abelian data $a$ in a residual subset of $A$;* 2. *for each such $a$, an actual section pencil in a residual subset of each prescribed nonempty admissible pencil open meeting $Q$;* 3. *after that pencil is fixed, all but countably many points of its intersection with $Q$ and with a nonempty algebraic good open.* *The selected points avoid the prescribed period loci. The geometric requirements hold on the algebraic good open, and the exceptional points for proper marked rational Hodge-tensor conditions on its whole connected smooth part form a countable set. The pencils in (ii) have the form $d_t=d_0+td_1$ with $\ell(d_0)=1$ and $\ell(d_1)=0$, and their leading section $d_1$ is smooth and avoids two-torsion. The final countable subset may include any further countable exceptions arising after the pencil is fixed; no uniform exceptional list across pencils is required.

Choose the abelian data and the pencil $d_t=d_0+t d_1$ in the generic sets of Lemma 16. There is a nonempty algebraic open $O\subset\mathbf A^1_t$ and a smooth projective family of K3 surfaces $S^0\to O$ with a flat isometric embedding of rational Hodge variations $$U\ \hookrightarrow\ R^2(S^0/O)_*\mathbb Q.$$ The form on $U$ here is its cup-product form inherited from $Y$. For very general $t$, this summand is the transcendental part of $H^2(S^0_t,\mathbb Q)$. For every $s$ in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of $\mathbf A^1_s$, every smooth projective model of the total family obtained by $t=s+u^2$ is uniruled. The K3 family over $O$ is defined over the original $t$-line; an additional unspecified finite base change is not part of the conclusion.

Let $V$ be an even lattice of signature $(2,14)$ with elementary $2$-primary discriminant group. Suppose a group $G\subset O(V)$ acts trivially on that group. There are an even finite-index overlattice $M$ of $V$, a primitive embedding $M\hookrightarrow\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}}$, and a primitive vector $h\in M^\perp$ with $(h,h)>0$, such that the action of $G$ extends to $\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}}$ and is the identity on $M^\perp$.

At every finite singular parameter of this general pencil, the monodromy on $V$ is a product of reflections in mutually orthogonal integral $(-2)$-roots in $V$. These roots are perpendicular to the limiting Hodge line. The periods extend to interior periods after killing these finite monodromies. At infinity the monodromy on $V$ is $-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}$.

Let $\mathscr P_h=[\Gamma_h\backslash\mathscr D_h]$, and let $\mathscr M_h$ denote the moduli stack of primitively polarized ADE K3 surfaces of degree $(h,h)$. There is a morphism $$q:\mathscr P_h\longrightarrow\mathscr M_h$$ whose composition with the period map of quasi-polarized smooth K3 surfaces is their canonical polarized contraction. The pullback of the Hodge line of $\mathscr M_h$ is the tautological period line, including its $\Gamma_h$-linearization.*

*For $[\sigma]\in\mathscr D_h$, let $W_\sigma$ be generated by the reflections in the roots $$R_\sigma=\{r\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}}:r^2=-2,\ (r,h)=0,\ (r,\sigma)=0\}.$$ The kernel of the homomorphism on stabilizers induced by $q$ is exactly $W_\sigma$.

Let $C$ be a smooth projective complex curve, let $D\subset C$ be finite, and put $C^\circ=C\setminus D$. Suppose the following data are given:* 1. *a local system $\mathcal L$ of lattices isometric to $\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}}$, with a primitive flat section $h$ of positive square;* 2. *a holomorphic line $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_{C^\circ}$ with $$(\mathcal F,\mathcal F)=0,\qquad (\sigma,\overline\sigma)>0\quad(0\ne\sigma\in\mathcal F),\qquad (\mathcal F,h)=0;$$* 3. *finite local monodromy at every point of $D$, and an interior limit of the period line after a local cover killing that monodromy.* *Then there is a normal projective model $f:\mathcal Z\to C$ whose restriction to $C^\circ$ is a family of polarized ADE K3 surfaces realizing these integral period data modulo contracted roots.* *Suppose, in addition, that the local monodromy at each $c\in D$, viewed on the limiting marked lattice, belongs to the Weyl group generated by $$R_c=\{r\in\mathcal L_c:r^2=-2,\ (r,h)=0,\ (r,\mathcal F_c)=0\}. \tag{\(*\)}\label{pencil:rootcondition}$$ Then $\mathcal Z\to C$ can be chosen to be a flat family of polarized ADE K3 surfaces on all of $C$. Its extended Hodge line descends to a line bundle $\lambda$ on $C$, and $$\omega_{\mathcal Z/C}\simeq f^*\lambda, \qquad K_{\mathcal Z}=f^*(K_C\otimes\lambda). \label{pencil:canonical}$$* *Under hypotheses (i)–(iii), independently of [pencil:rootcondition], let $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal L_\mathbb Q$ be a nondegenerate rational sub-local system containing $\mathcal F$, and suppose every flat root which is of type $(1,1)$ on an open set is perpendicular to $\mathcal U$. After shrinking a nonempty algebraic open in $C^\circ$, there is a smooth projective K3 family $\mathcal S^0$ there and an identification of $\mathcal U$ with an isometric Hodge summand of $R^2\mathcal S^0_*\mathbb Q$. Here a flat root means a locally flat section; it need not be a globally invariant vector. No change of the base curve occurs in this conclusion.
Under the Weyl condition of Lemma 21, suppose $\deg(K_C\otimes\lambda)<0$. Every smooth projective model of the function field of $\mathcal Z$ is uniruled.

Let $O\subset\mathbf A^1_t$ be a nonempty Zariski open set, and let $$f:\mathcal S\longrightarrow O,
 \qquad g:\mathcal X\longrightarrow O$$ be smooth projective families of connected surfaces, with the fibers of $f$ K3 surfaces. Suppose that the following conditions hold.*

1.  *A polarized rational subvariation $\mathscr U\subset R^2f_*\mathbb Q$ of K3 type, with nondegenerate restricted cup product, is given. Its period map is nonconstant, and $U_t=\mathscr U_t$ is simple for all but countably many $t\in O$.*

2.  *There are commuting involutions $j,\delta$ of $\mathcal X$ over $O$ such that $$e=\tfrac14(1+j)(1-\delta)$$ annihilates $R^qg_*\mathbb Q$ for $q\ne2$, together with an isomorphism of rational variations of Hodge structure $$\varphi:\mathscr U\xrightarrow{\sim}eR^2g_*\mathbb Q.$$*

3.  *For $s$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset of $\mathbf A^1$, the total spaces of the two surface families pulled back by $t=s+u^2$ have smooth projective uniruled threefold models.*

*Then there are a nonempty Zariski open set $G\subset O$ and a countable set $E\subset G$ such that, for every $b\in G\setminus E$, a correspondence $$\Theta_b\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S_b\times X_b)_\mathbb Q$$ induces $\varphi_b$ on $U_b$. The open set $G$ and all auxiliary correspondences used before the choice of $b$ can be fixed for the given pencil.

If $Z$ is a smooth projective uniruled threefold over $\mathbb C$, then $H^3(Z)$ is a direct summand of a finite sum of spaces $H^1(C_i)(-1)$, with both maps of the splitting induced by algebraic correspondences. Consequently, every rational Hodge map between the third cohomologies of two such threefolds is algebraic.

Let $B$ be a smooth affine complex curve.*

1.  *A bounded complex on $B$ with finite-rank local-system cohomology only in even degrees has a unique splitting as the direct sum of its cohomology sheaves, shifted to their degrees, inducing the identity on each cohomology sheaf.*

2.  *If $A$ is a bounded complex with local-system cohomology, then there is a natural exact sequence $$0\longrightarrow H^1(B,\mathcal H^{n-1}A)
     \longrightarrow \mathbb H^n(B,A)
     \longrightarrow H^0(B,\mathcal H^nA)\longrightarrow0.$$ For a morphism of such complexes, its action on the left-hand term is determined by its action on $\mathcal H^{n-1}$.

Let $I$ be a smooth affine curve, let $h_S:E^S\to I$ be a smooth projective K3 family, and let $h_X:E^X\to I$ be a smooth projective surface family with a relative algebraic idempotent $e$ acting on the direct-image complex whose action on $R^q h_{X*}\mathbb Q$ vanishes for $q\ne2$. Suppose that $$a:R^2h_{S*}\mathbb Q\longrightarrow eR^2h_{X*}\mathbb Q$$ is a morphism of rational Hodge variations. Let $Z^S,Z^X$ be smooth projective compactifications which extend the two maps to a smooth projective compactification of $I$ and are unchanged over $I$. Write $\overline I$ for that compactified curve. There is a rational Hodge map $c:H^3(Z^S)\to H^3(Z^X)$ satisfying $$e\,\operatorname{res}_X(cz)
   =H^1(I,a)\bigl(\operatorname{res}_S z\bigr),
 \qquad z\in H^3(Z^S),$$ where $H^3(E^S)$ and $eH^3(E^X)$ are identified canonically with $H^1(I,R^2h_{S*}\mathbb Q)$ and $H^1(I,eR^2h_{X*}\mathbb Q)$.

For a smooth projective surface family $\mathcal Y\to O$, its first square pullbacks admit models $Z$ projective over $\mathbf A^1_s$ and a nonempty open set $G\subset O$ such that $Z_G\to G$ is smooth. These models may be chosen with the following additional property. For every $b\in G$ there is a smooth projective fourfold $M_b$, with morphisms to $\mathbf P^1_t$ and $\mathbf P^1_v$, whose inverse images of $V_0\subset\mathbf P^1_v$ and $O\subset\mathbf P^1_t$ are, respectively,*

1.  *$Z_G\times_GV_0$, where $V_0\to G$ is $v\mapsto b+v^2$ and $V_0=\{v\in\mathbf A^1:b+v^2\in G\}$;*

2.  *$\mathcal Y\times_OQ_b$, where $$\label{comp:conic}
     Q_b=\{u^2+v^2=(t-b)w^2\}\subset O\times\mathbf P^2.$$*

*The two identifications agree on their intersection. In particular, both specified spaces are preserved as actual open subvarieties. Shrinking $G$ before choosing $b$ preserves these conclusions.

Fix abelian-cover data and a section pencil for which [geom:structure](#geom:structure), [geom:period](#geom:period), [pencil:realization](#pencil:realization) apply, with nonconstant $U$-period along the pencil and simple $U_t$ outside a countable set. On a nonempty open of that pencil, for all but countably many $b$, there is an algebraic correspondence $$\Theta_b\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S_b^0\times X_b)_\mathbb Q$$ whose action on $U_b$ is the given identification with $H^2(X_b)^{j=+,\,\delta=-}$.

Choose the abelian data and the pencil as in Lemma 16, and then choose $b$ in the common good open outside the countable exceptional sets of that lemma and Corollary 28. Then there are smooth projective curves $C_1,C_2$ and a rational algebraic correspondence $$Z\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S_b^0\times C_1\times C_2)_{\mathbb Q}$$ whose action restricts to an injection $$f:U_b\longrightarrow H^1(C_1,\mathbb Q)\otimes H^1(C_2,\mathbb Q).$$ Here $U_b=T_{S_b^0}$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hg}}(U_b)=\mathop{\mathrm{SO}}(U_b)$.

Let $(U,q)$ be an eight-dimensional polarized rational Hodge structure of K3 type, of signature $(2,6)$, and suppose $\mathop{\mathrm{Hg}}(U)=\mathop{\mathrm{SO}}(U,q)$. Let $W_1,W_2$ be polarized effective weight-one Hodge structures and let $W=C^+(U,q)$ have its Kuga–Satake Hodge structure. For every nonzero Hodge map $$f:U\longrightarrow W_1\otimes W_2,$$ put $$\mathcal H=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{HS}}(W_1,W)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}
       \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{HS}}(W_2,W).$$ If $\tau:W\otimes W\to W\otimes W$ is the ordinary tensor flip, the rational linear map $$\Phi:\mathcal H\oplus\mathcal H\longrightarrow
       \mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{HS}}(U,W\otimes W),$$ defined by $$\begin{cases}
 \Phi(a\otimes b,0)=(a\otimes b)\circ f,\\
 \Phi(0,a\otimes b)=\tau\circ(a\otimes b)\circ f
 \end{cases}$$ is surjective.*

*If $U\subset H^2(M,\mathbb Q)$ for a smooth projective surface $M$, $W_i=H^1(C_i,\mathbb Q)$, $W=H^1(A,\mathbb Q)$, and $f$ is the restriction of a codimension-two algebraic correspondence from $M$ to $C_1\times C_2$, then every map in the target of $\Phi$ is induced by a cycle in $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(M\times A\times A)_\mathbb Q$.

Let $b$ be a construction point of Lemma 29, and let $S$ be a projective K3 surface equipped with a rational Hodge isometry $r_T:T_S\xrightarrow{\sim}U_b=T_{S_b^0}$ for the cup-product forms. For every full even-Clifford model $A$ of $T_S$, every rational nonisotropic right factor $w$, and every rational polarization $E$, there is a cycle $$\Gamma_S\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S\times A\times A)_\mathbb Q, \qquad (\Gamma_S)_*x=\iota_{w,E}(x)\quad(x\in T_S),$$ where the equality holds in $H^2(A\times A,\mathbb Q)$.

Buskin’s theorem does not require integrality or preservation of an ample chamber. In its cyclic reduction, order one means an integral isometry. After a possible sign change and finitely many reflections in algebraic $(-2)$-classes, it maps a Kähler chamber to a Kähler chamber, so strong Torelli realizes it by an isomorphism; its graph and the sign and reflection correspondences are algebraic. In the final rational-reflection chain, transport an initial integral ample class through the partial isometries. On each intermediate period-realized K3 it is a rational $(1,1)$-class of positive square. Clearing denominators gives an integral such class, so the K3 projectivity criterion makes every intermediate surface projective, as required for the cyclic steps.

Let $S$ have an ample primitive $P$-polarization and put $U_P=P_{\mathbb Q}^{\perp}\subset H^2(S,\mathbb Q)$. There are a full even-Clifford realization $W_U=C^+(U_P,q)=H^1(A_U,\mathbb Q)$, a rational polarization $E_0$, a nonisotropic rational $w_0\in U_P$, and a cycle $$\Gamma_U\in\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^2(S\times A_U^2)_{\mathbb Q}$$ whose full degree-two action on every $x\in U_P$ is exactly $\iota_{w_0,E_0}(x)$. This assertion concerns the whole fixed rank-eight space, including its rational $(1,1)$ classes at a Picard jump.

Let $(V,q)$ be a rational quadratic space of signature $(2,n)$. The group $O(V)(\mathbb Q)$ is dense in $O(V_{\mathbb R})$, and the rational orbit of every point of its type-IV period domain meets every nonempty open subset of that domain.

Let $i:W_T\hookrightarrow W_U$ be an inclusion of polarizable rational weight-one Hodge structures, let $p:W_U\to W_T$ be a Hodge retraction, and let $E_U,E_T$ be rational polarizations. Let $H$ be a rational Hodge structure of weight zero. For a Hodge map $j:H\to\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(W_U)$, write $\iota_{j,E_U}:H(-1)\to W_U\otimes W_U$ for its tensor form. Set $$b=(E_T^\flat)^{-1}i^\vee(-1)E_U^\flat:W_U\longrightarrow W_T.$$ Then $$\label{transfer:compression-identity}
 (p\otimes b)\iota_{j,E_U}=\iota_{pji,E_T}.$$ If the weight-one structures are abelian $H^1$ spaces, both maps on the tensor slots are induced by rational algebraic correspondences.

Let $S$ be an ample $P$-polarized K3 surface. For every prescribed nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, rational polarization $E$ and transported even-Clifford realization of $C^+(T_S,q)$, its standard tensor $\iota_{w,E}$ has a rational codimension-two algebraic realization.

Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface with a rational isometric embedding $\iota:T_S\hookrightarrow V_P$. There is an ample $P$-polarized K3 surface $R$ and a full rational Hodge isometry $$\Phi:H^2(S,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(R,\mathbb Q),\qquad
 \Phi(T_S)=T_R.$$ Both directions of this isometry are induced by algebraic correspondences.
Under the isometric-embedding hypothesis of Theorem 2, the exact tensor $\iota_{w,E}$ on $T_S$ is algebraic for every stipulated $w$, $E$, and transported isogenous even-Clifford model.

Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface admitting a rational isometric embedding $(T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P$. For every $n,r\ge1$, rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of $(S^{[n]})^r$, where $S^{[n]}$ is the Hilbert scheme of length-$n$ subschemes of $S$.*

*More generally, let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Br}(S)$ and let $M$ be either a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker-stable $\alpha$-twisted sheaves on $S$, or a smooth projective moduli space of $\sigma$-stable objects in $D^b(S,\alpha)$ for a generic Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma$. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of $M^r$ for every $r\ge1$. If $M$ is hyperkähler, the same conclusions hold for every smooth projective hyperkähler variety birational to $M$ and all its self-powers.
